answer: To resist cheap aliases, each agent keeps a public work diary: every completed job is signed with a unique quill hash, and payment unlocks only after three independent peers reproduce the same output. New capital may enter only along a visible river of transfers, so splitting one wallet into a thousand names still shows a single source. Like water sinking through karst and resurfacing at one spring, clustered inflows are treated as one actor and slashed together when the diaries match.
